goals.title: Build with the waves
goals.critique: This is round 4's 'Teach the sea to build' again, and it finally fixes the slow loop: a wave every few seconds that leaves a stripe you can read, so each move is answered before the next one. The evening tide and a stranded Pickles give each day a clock and a reason. Two things undercut it. If a stripe lands visibly behind a stone every wave, the stones are close to a paint brush and the sea stops feeling like a real coast. And once Lumi can also dig and press sand with its feet, the pitch never says why the player wouldn't just build the bridge by hand, which would erase the indirect verb that makes this candidate its own. Pickles being 'stranded' is also left vague: nothing says what that costs or what happens next, so the stakes are a picture rather than a consequence. The road is in the right order, starting with a filmed surf box, but per-wave deposition that is fast, legible and still physical is the whole bet and remains unproven.

goals.title: A bridge the friends trust
goals.critique: This one sits closest to what the human asked for: gathered materials that behave by what they are (green hazel bends, driftwood snaps, wet rope stretches), Lumi's beak doing the tying, and things that stay and get used by the friends every day. The heavy pig sagging the middle until a dry stick cracks is a clip people would send. But load-testing a bridge you built is a well-established genre, and gathered sticks plus a creature as the test weight is a variation on it, not a new mechanic. 'Trust' is the word in the title and it is never defined: nothing says what makes a friend refuse or step on, so the one new idea is still a label. Play risks shrinking to one stream, then the same problem made longer, and tying knots with a beak in first person could turn fiddly long before it feels skilful. The road starts in the right place, one stick that bends or snaps by its wood, and every step after it is something to play with on its own.
